text:
jordan-sales: Quick sync — Mosaic POC looks good but procurement just pushed back on payment reserve language in the order form. They attached a redline and are asking who signs and whether we can narrow the holdback to milestone-based release. Can legal + procurement confirm acceptable wording and signer path?
prateek-se: Thanks. From a POC standpoint we can support milestone release (go-live verification) — need billing team ok on net terms.
sara-legal: I skimmed the redline. Two quick asks: 1) remove open-ended escrow wording, 2) change ‘holdback’ to ‘reserve payment’ and tie release to an acceptance checklist. Draft below.
sara-legal: ```Suggested clause: "Customer may reserve up to 15% of the total Order Form value pending completion of the Acceptance Checklist. Redwood will release reserved funds within 10 business days of mutual written confirmation of acceptance. No escrow account required."```
chris-procurement: If we accept 15% and checklist, finance needs workflow. Who signs the Order Form? Customer has separate procurement signer (PO team) and legal exec for the MSA. We need one embedded esign path for both.
jordan-sales: @chris-procurement who on our side needs to countersign? Usually account exec + finance ops. For Mosaic they prefer a single envelope to reduce delays.
chris-procurement: On our side: AE (jordan-sales) + Finance Ops (finance-ops@redwood) or delegated signer. Can procurement create the esign envelope?
prateek-se: One technical note — the acceptance checklist should include a smoke test + latency under 200ms for 95th percentile and sample quality checks. Put that in the checklist so acceptance is measurable.
sara-legal: Good call. I'll add a short acceptance bullet list. Also recommend adding: "If parties fail to agree on acceptance within 15 days, the default is release upon customer confirmation of production traffic."
jordan-sales: Here's a tiny orderform snippet they asked to see, pasted for visibility:
```
OrderFormItem: Mosaic POC
Term: 12 months
Total: $120,000
Reserve: 15% tied to Acceptance Checklist
Billing: Net30
```
chris-procurement: Ok — procurement can create the DocuSign envelope once legal confirms final clause. Who will be on the envelope from customer side? I think both PO team and Head of Procurement.
sara-legal: Confirmed clause below; fine to proceed unless someone sees a blocker.
sara-legal: "Reserve Payment: Customer may withhold up to 15% of fees until completion of the Acceptance Checklist. Redwood will invoice reserved amounts upon mutual acceptance or 30 days after production traffic begins if no dispute is raised."
jordan-sales: @ops-bot can you create an esign request flow for `mosaic-poc-OF-2025` with signers: Mosaic PO, Mosaic Head of Procurement, Jordan (AE), Finance Ops?
ops-bot: Created envelope ID env_2025_3348 — status: draft. Tagging legal to review first. :white_check_mark:
chris-procurement: I'll add finance-ops@redwood to the envelope and route after legal sign-off.
prateek-se: One more: we should include acceptance test owners and a one-page checklist in the envelope as an attachment. I'll upload the test plan to the ticket.
sara-legal: I approve the language for routing. If procurement wants to tighten the days (10 vs 30) call it out — otherwise I'm OK with 30 as fallback.
jordan-sales: Great — next steps: sara will paste final clause into order form, chris will create final envelope and add attachments, prateek will upload checklist. I'll follow up with Mosaic to confirm their signer emails. :thumbsup:
chris-procurement: On it, target to send envelope to customer by EOD tomorrow.
sara-legal: Reviewed and added clause to OF draft. Please ping if Mosaic proposes any non-standard escrow language.
jordan-sales: Thanks everyone. Noted — I'll update the deal in Salesforce after envelope sent. :eyes:
